name.text: Estimating the combined mean and standard deviation for two datasets presented as dotplots

questiontext.text:
The dot plots below show the weights of samples of male and female birds of the same species. Can you estimate the mean and standard deviation if the male and female birds were combined?

[[jsxgraph]] // Create empty list of points var p = []; // Create board var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, { boundingbox: [{#xmin#}, {#ymax#}, {#xmax#}, {#ymin#}], keepaspectratio: false, showCopyright: false, axis:true }); //Create points of Data Set 2 var lx2 = {#dorx2#}; var ly2 = {#dory2#}; var i = 0; for (i = 0; i <= lx2.length - 1; i++) { p[i] = board.create('point', [lx2[i], ly2[i]], { face: 'x', name: '', size: 2, fixed:true }); } //Create Label for Data 2 var txt = board.create('text', [{#xmin#}+1, {#maxfreq2#}/2+2, "Male"], { fontSize: 30,fixed: true }); //Create points of Data Set 1 var lx1 = {#dorx1#}; var ly1 = {#dory1#}; var i = 0; for (i = 0; i <= lx1.length - 1; i++) { p[i] = board.create('point', [lx1[i], ly1[i]], { face: 'x', name: '', size: 2, fixed:true }); } //Create Label for Data 1 var txt = board.create('text', [{#xmin#}+1, {#maxfreq1#}/2+{#maxfreq2#} + 5, "Female"], { fontSize: 30,fixed: true }); [[/jsxgraph]]

Estimated combined mean of the male and female birds? [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

Estimated combined standard deviation of male and female birds? [[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

generalfeedback.text:
To estimate the combined mean, imagine merging the two dotplots into a single distribution. Look for a plausible value for the mean by considering how far the observations lie above and below it. Observations further from the mean should have more influence on your estimate than observations close to it.

To estimate the combined standard deviation, consider the distances of all the observations from your estimated combined mean. Look for a value that represents a typical spread around the mean, remembering that observations far from the mean have a greater effect on the standard deviation.

questionnote.text: sd1 = {@sd1@}, sd2 = {@sd2@}. mean1 = {@mean1@}, mean2 = {@mean2@}. ta1= {@ta1@}, ta2 = {@ta2@}

prtcorrect.text: Correct answer, well done.

prtpartiallycorrect.text: Your answer is partially correct.

prtincorrect.text: Incorrect answer.

truefeedback.text: Well done, your estimate is within 10% of the combined mean.
Good estimate. You are within 25% of the combined mean. See if you can refine your estimate.

falsefeedback.text: Your estimate is not close enough. Look again at the values in both groups and consider how all the observations contribute to the combined mean.

truefeedback.text: Well done, your estimate is within 10% of the combined standard deviation.
Good estimate. You are within 25% of the combined standard deviation. See if you can refine your estimate.

falsefeedback.text: Your estimate is not close enough. Consider how far observations in both groups lie from the combined mean.
